page.desc: The Olight ArkPro Ultra and Wuben X5 each come in a Class 1 and a Class 3R laser version under the same name, and laser power differs by up to 13×. We compare their laser class, mW and step-down output with Klein, Fenix and Wurkkos, plus today's store prices.
page.answer: Short answer. The best flashlight with laser pointer is the Olight ArkPro Ultra in its Class 3R version: a rechargeable flashlight with a built-in green laser rated up to 5 mW, 13× its 0.39 mW Class 1 twin sold under the same name. The Wuben X5 3R is the swappable-battery pick.

page.after:
What the differences mean

  • Same name, two lasers. The ArkPro Ultra's Class 3R version is rated up to 5 mW and its Class 1 version 0.39 mW: 5 ÷ 0.39 = 12.8×.
  • Green work light vs green EDC light. Wuben states 3 mW for the X5 3R. Klein states under 1 mW for the 56074: 3 ÷ 1 = more than 3×. Against the ArkPro Ultra 3R's 5 mW rating, the Klein's ceiling is under 1 ÷ 5 = one-fifth.
  • Laser runtime. ArkPro Ultra 3R 50 h vs Wuben X5 3R 24 h: 50 ÷ 24 = 2.1×. In the Class 1 versions it is 226 h vs 50 h.
  • White light once turbo ends. On claimed peaks the ArkPro Ultra leads the Klein 56074 by 1,700 ÷ 1,000 = 1.7×. Once both settle, Olight's 520 lm against Klein's 400 lm High is 520 ÷ 400 = 1.3×. The Wuben X5 also settles at about 400 lm (roma58 measured), so 520 ÷ 400 = 1.3× there too.
  • Light per X5 charge. 400 lm × (100 min ÷ 60) = about 670 lumen-hours from one 4.44 Wh pack. A spare pack doubles it.
  • X5 on AAA. Turbo drops to 850 lm: 850 ÷ 1,300 = 65%. Wuben's table keeps High 350 lm, Medium 150 lm and Low 50 lm the same as on the pack.

Same name, two lasers: check the class on the box

A laser's class sets its power ceiling: Class 2 visible lasers are limited to 1 mW and Class 3R to 5 mW. How bright the dot looks is that power times the eye's sensitivity at the laser's wavelength. On the CIE photopic table, that sensitivity is 0.710 at 520 nm (green) and 0.107 at 650 nm (red). At equal power a 520 nm green dot looks 0.710 ÷ 0.107 = 6.6× brighter than a 650 nm red one. Put the class ceilings together and a 5 mW green Class 3R (5 × 0.710 = 3.55) looks about 33× brighter than a 1 mW, 650 nm red (1 × 0.107).

Olight sells the ArkPro Ultra as a Class 1 version (0.39 mW, 226 h of laser) and a Class 3R version (5 mW, 50 h), both under the same model name. Which one you get depends on the SKU. Wuben does the same with the X5. On Wuben's US store both versions cost $79.99 (2026-11-08), so the stronger laser costs nothing extra: {buy:wuben-x5-3-in-1-class-3r}. Wuben's product text, as quoted by BudgetLightForum reviewer worrub918, limits the 3R version to buyers in the US and Canada. Elsewhere the Class 1 version is the one on offer: {buy:wuben-x5-3-in-1-class-1}.

Measured against claims: 1lumen (Nick) read the Olight ArkPro at 1,372 lm at 30 s against its 1,500 lm claim (91%). 1lumen (Rob) read the Wurkkos HD01 Pro at 1,023 lm against 1,200 lm (85%), then 428 lm at 10 min and 1 h 02 min in total. In the same integrating sphere, the HD01 Pro's green laser read 9 lux against 5 lux for Olight's Arkfeld Pro and Ultra, which is a relative reading, not mW. 1lumen gives no laser class for it, and Wurkkos's own store listing was offline when we checked on 2026-11-08, so it has no row above. BudgetLightForum's roma58 measured the Wuben X5 holding about 400 lm for about 100 min after turbo, and High (350 lm) running just over 2 h.

Not recommended

Klein Tools 56074 for long-distance pointing. It is sold as a green-laser work light, but Klein rates the laser Class 2, under 1 mW. That is at most a fifth of a Class 3R rating, enough to point inside a room or across a job box. Fenix E06R if you want the laser to show up: its laser is red, and at equal power a 650 nm red dot looks 6.6× dimmer than a 520 nm green one. Fenix's green-laser model in the same family is the E06R PRO RG ($84.95, 2026-11-08). Never point any of these lasers at eyes, vehicles or aircraft.
